text: DSH-Idle-Watchdog 是面向 DSH web 的会话提醒插件，会在用户选择监测的聊天长时间无活动且 agent 空闲时发送后续提示，并提供可由脚本调用的 HTTP 提示接口。它通过 DSH 会话事件判断活动状态，在设置页配置全局和单个聊天的提醒窗口、提示词与次数上限；也可按会话编号、编号前缀或标题投递消息。外部接口使用共享密钥，未使用接口时无需配置该密钥。

DSH-Idle-Watchdog nudges opted-in DSH web chats after a configured idle window. Users can set prompts and limits in Settings. Scripts can send a message to a chat through its HTTP endpoint using a session ID or title. The endpoint can resume cold chats when enabled and requires a shared secret.
想让已选中的 DSH 会话在闲置一段时间后自动收到提醒。
DSH 聊天停住没继续时，能不能按每个会话设置不同的跟进提示和等待时间？
How can a scheduled script send a prompt into one of my DSH chats by its title or session ID?
DSH-Idle-Watchdog 的功能「闲置会话提醒」：为聊天单独启用监测后，在 agent 空闲且超过静默窗口时发送提示；达到次数上限后等待用户回复。
DSH-Idle-Watchdog 的功能「HTTP 会话提示」：向 `/dsh-idle-watchdog/api/prompt` 提交会话编号或标题及消息，由服务端将提示发送到对应聊天。
DSH-Idle-Watchdog 使用 prompt API 前需设置共享密钥，可通过环境变量、专用密钥文件或设置项提供；未配置密钥时该 API 不接受提示请求。

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com) (DSH) web-profile plugin with two jobs:
section: restart dsh web, then opt chats in under Settings, Idle Watchdog

text:
dsh-idle-watchdog README · restart dsh web, then opt chats in under Settings, Idle Watchdog：1. **Idle nudges.** Chats you opt in are watched. When one goes quiet for longer than your idle window and its agent is idle, the watchdog posts a followup prompt into that same chat, up to a cap, until you reply.
2. **External prompt API.** One small, secret-protected HTTP endpoint lets scripts, cron jobs, webhooks or another machine post a message into any chat by id, id-prefix or exact title, waking a cold (not loaded) chat through DSH's own resume path when you allow it.
section: restart dsh web, then opt chats in under Settings, Idle Watchdog

text: dsh-idle-watchdog README · Why：Long autonomous chats stall for boring reasons: the model stopped after a plan, a tool call failed, a rate limit ended a turn, or the agent simply asked "shall I continue?" while you were away. The watchdog nudges such a chat back to work, with a cap so it never loops forever, and quiet hours and backoff so it stays polite. The API is the other half: anything that is not a human can still talk to a chat (a nightly job finishing, a CI webhook, a monitoring alert) without you building your own session plumbing.

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Install (DSH web profile)：Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-idle-watchdog`, or from GitHub: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/DSH-Idle-Watchdog`.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-idle-watchdog

dsh-idle-watchdog README · then restart dsh-web: the host half is mounted at boot only：```

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists `dsh-idle-watchdog` in `dsh.profile.bundles`.

Or from a local checkout (linked, not copied: keep the checkout where it lives):bash
git clone https://github.com/lucagiftzek/DSH-Idle-Watchdog ~/plugins/DSH-Idle-Watchdog
cd ~/plugins/DSH-Idle-Watchdog && pnpm install      # or npm install

text: dsh-idle-watchdog README · Configuration：Everything is in **Settings, Idle Watchdog**, and applies live. Where it is stored depends on the DSH line:

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Configuration：* **DSH 0.1.5 and older:** the `dsh-idle-watchdog` namespace of `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` (hand-editable).
* **DSH 0.1.7 / 0.2.x and newer:** the plugin row `idle-watchdog` in the profile patch, `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (`- id: idle-watchdog` / `config:`). On the first boot after an upgrade the old `dsh-idle-watchdog` section is imported once from `settings.yaml.imported`, never over a row that already has values.
* **No settings service:** `~/.dsh/idle-watchdog/settings.json`.
dsh-idle-watchdog README · Configuration：`/status` reports which store is active (`settingsStore`: `settings`, `profile-row` or `fallback-file`).

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Configuration：**API secret file.** The prompt API secret has a version-independent home: `~/.dsh/idle-watchdog/api-secret` (mode 0600; override the path with `DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_SECRET_FILE`). Precedence: env `DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_SECRET`, then the file, then the stored `api.secret` setting. Saving a secret in Settings writes the file; on 0.2.x the secret never goes into the profile patch, and the upgrade import moves an old `api.secret` into the file. Scripts read it with `IW_SECRET=${DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_SECRET:-$(cat ~/.dsh/idle-watchdog/api-secret)}`.

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Configuration：| Setting | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | Master switch (per-chat opt-in is still required) | `true` |
| `idleMinutes` | Minutes of silence before a nudge (1 to 10080) | `20` |
| `maxNudges` | Nudges per idle period; your reply refills the budget (0 to 20, 0 = never nudge) | `3` |
| `tickSeconds` | How often the watchdog scans (5 to 3600) | `30` |
| `defaultPrompt` | Text posted when a chat has no prompt of its own | a short English nudge |
| `notifyOnCap` | Post one folded notice when the cap is hit | `true` |
| `chats` | Watched chats: `id`, `label`, `enabled`, `prompt` (override), `idleMinutes` (override, 0 = global) | none watched |
| `api.secret` | Shared secret for the prompt API; unset means the API fails closed | unset |
| `api.rateLimitPerMinute` | Prompt calls per minute per source IP (1 to 600) | `30` |
| `wakeColdForApi` | API may resume a chat that is not currently loaded | `true` |
| `skipWhenGoalActive` | Never nudge a chat whose goal-round driver is armed and active | `false` |
| `onlyAfterError` | Nudge only after the agent reported an error since the last human message | `false` |
| `backoffFactor` | Windo

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Configuration：The behaviour options added in 1.1 (`skipWhenGoalActive`, `onlyAfterError`, backoff, quiet hours) default to the old behaviour, so upgrading changes nothing until you opt in. Quiet hours delay nudges only; the external API is never blocked by them.

Example `settings.yaml` fragment:

```yaml
dsh-idle-watchdog:
  enabled: true
  idleMinutes: 15
  maxNudges: 4

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Nudge semantics：A watched chat is nudged when all of these hold: the master switch is on, the chat is enabled, its agent is **live and idle** (a running turn is never interrupted), no active goal round if `skipWhenGoalActive` is on (needs the `goals` service; if your DSH lacks it the option is a no-op), an error was seen if `onlyAfterError` is on, the cap is not reached, the silence since the **last append of any kind** (including the watchdog's own previous nudge) exceeds the window (multiplied by the backoff for the n-th nudge), and quiet hours are not active. A human message resets the counter and the error flag. Reaching the cap posts one folded notice (not a fake user turn) and waits for you. Cold chats are never woken for idle reasons; only the API can wake them.
dsh-idle-watchdog README · Nudge semantics：State survives restarts (`~/.dsh/idle-watchdog/state.json`, atomic writes). The audit ledger is `~/.dsh/idle-watchdog/activity.jsonl` (rolling, 512 KiB).

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Seeing what happens next：The Status card in Settings shows, per watched chat, the next nudge time or the reason it is held (running, goal active, quiet hours, cap reached, waiting for an error), the last outcome and the nudge count. The same data is a read-only endpoint, so you can preview without sending anything:

```bash
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-idle-watchdog/api/next
```

dsh-idle-watchdog README · The HTTP API：`POST /dsh-idle-watchdog/api/prompt`, JSON body:

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | yes | exact session id, **unique** id prefix (6 or more chars, live or watched chats), or exact chat title / Settings label |
| `message` | yes | up to 8000 chars; arrives as a user-role message from plugin `dsh-idle-watchdog` |
| `provenance` | no | up to 80 chars of free label recorded in the audit ledger (for example `cron-backup`) |

dsh-idle-watchdog README · The HTTP API：Auth, one of: `x-idle-watchdog-secret: <secret>` or `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.

```bash

dsh-idle-watchdog README · set the secret once in Settings (or export DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_SECRET for dsh-web), then:：IW_SECRET=${DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_SECRET:-$(cat ~/.dsh/idle-watchdog/api-secret)}
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-idle-watchdog/api/prompt \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H "x-idle-watchdog-secret: $IW_SECRET" \
  -d '{"chat":"ops triage","message":"Recheck the queue and alert on regressions.","provenance":"cron"}'

text:
dsh-idle-watchdog README · from another machine you can ssh into：| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `202` | delivered to a live chat |
| `200` | delivered after resuming a cold chat |
| `400` | validation error |
| `401` | wrong secret (10 failures per minute per IP, then `429`) |
| `403` | the chat is owned by a subagent |
| `404` | unknown chat |
| `409` | ambiguous reference, or the chat cannot be delivered to (cold with `wakeColdForApi` off) |
| `429` | rate limited, see `retry-after` |
| `503` | no secret configured (fail closed) |

text:
dsh-idle-watchdog README · Security notes：* DSH mounts plugin routes **without host authentication**. The socket is loopback, so the secret is the control for machine callers. If you expose DSH through a reverse proxy, put the route behind your login proxy as well and do not publish it bare.
* Use a long random secret (16 to 256 characters). Prefer the `DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_SECRET` environment variable of the dsh-web process: it wins over the stored value and keeps the secret off disk. Rotate it by setting a new one; the UI shows only an 8-hex fingerprint.
* The secret is compared in constant time (sha256 then `timingSafeEqual`) and is never logged or returned. `GET /status` masks it.
* A browser cross-site JSON POST cannot work: the custom header forces a CORS preflight and no CORS headers are ever sent. UI-mutating routes also require `X-Requested-With: dsh-idle-watchdog` and a JSON content type. Bodies are capped at 64 KiB.
* Anything that can post to a chat can steer an agent that has tools. Treat the secret like shell access to that agent.

dsh-idle-watchdog README · When something goes wrong：* Ask your agent to load the **`idle-watchdog-doctor`** skill. It ships in `skills/idle-watchdog-doctor/` and the plugin registers it with the skills service at start (offered after `dsh web` restarts). If your DSH does not list it, install it by hand:
  ```bash
  P=$(node -p "require('path').dirname(require.resolve('dsh-idle-watchdog/package.json',{paths:[(process.env.DSH_HOME||require('os').homedir()+'/.dsh')+'/profiles/web']}))")
  mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" && cp -r "$P/skills/idle-watchdog-doctor" "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/"
  ```
  The skills folder is watched, so it appears without a restart. Details: [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#start-here).
* One-call self-check: `GET /dsh-idle-watchdog/api/doctor` (read-only, same access as `/status`). It reports the settings mode, whether `Config` is visible to the loader, whether an API secret is configured (yes or no, plus its source: env, file or settings; never the value), the secret file mode (0600), the watched chats, `sessionController`, the next-nudge preview, the age of the last scan and whether the state file is writable. dsh-idle-watchdog README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| Route answers `404` | Package is not in the profile bundles yet, or dsh-web was not restarted after installing |
| `503 secret-not-configured` | Set a secret in Settings or export `DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_SECRET` for the dsh-web process |
| `401` then `429` | Wrong secret; wait for `retry-after` |
| No nudges arrive | Check the Status card: the chat must be enabled, live (loaded), idle, past its window, not capped, not in quiet hours, and (with `onlyAfterError`) have seen an error |
| Settings section missing | Hard-reload the page; the client half hot-reloads but needs the package in the profile |
| Settings are not saved to YAML | `/status` shows `settingsStore: fallback-file`; the settings service or schemastery could not be loaded |

dsh-idle-watchdog README · Troubleshooting：Operations: `GET /api/status` for full state, `GET /api/logs` for the ledger tail. To pause without a restart, switch *Enabled* off in Settings. Kill switch: add `- id: idle-watchdog` / `disabled: true` to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and restart, or set `DSH_IDLE_WATCHDOG_DISABLE=1` in the dsh-web environment.

dsh-idle-watchdog README · How it differs from related tools：* **DSH goal rounds (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver`).** A goal is an explicit objective the model works on across automatic rounds, with a round cap, and ends when the model marks it complete or blocked. It is the right tool when you can state an objective. The watchdog has no objective: it is a generic "you went quiet" prod for any opted-in chat, plus an outside entry point. Turn on `skipWhenGoalActive` so the two never both push the same chat.
* **Schedulers in the dsh-cron style.** A scheduler decides *when* to start a task at wall-clock times. The watchdog reacts to *silence*, not to the clock, and the prompt API is what a scheduler or system cron would call to deliver its message into an existing chat.
* **Watchers in the dsh-sentinel style.** A watcher observes a condition (files, services, metrics) and acts on it. The watchdog only watches chat activity. A watcher that wants to tell an agent something can use the prompt API.
